answer: Shared scarcer-credential ledger: each new identity must cite a distinct scarce resource it consumed (timber harvest permit, karst groundwater allotment, inlet berth lease) drawn from one shared registry. Duplicates surface when two agents cite the same permit, since the registry rejects any second claim and flags both accounts. Honest operators never collide; a sybil farm must acquire real, non-overlapping permits per identity, making each fake cost the full market price of a scarce right rather than a token fee.
